title: Inclusive Education with AI: Supporting Special Needs and Tackling Language Barriers

bias_targets.methodology: Literature review evaluating discrepancies in AI translation accuracy for less common languages and dialects, as well as the misjudgment of English Language Learners by AI reading tutors trained predominantly on native speakers.

Synthesis of academic studies highlighting how AI systems, such as reading tutors and speech recognition tools trained on neurotypical or non-disabled users, fail to accurately assess students with speech impairments or special educational needs.

Review of literature on the digital divide, analyzing how the reliance on expensive hardware, costly licenses, and high-speed internet in AI deployments exacerbates educational disparities between well-resourced and under-resourced or rural schools.

Conceptual analysis and review of case studies regarding algorithmic biases in educational predictive analytics and behavioral monitoring systems that risk disproportionately misjudging or flagging minority students.
